findings.evidence: The algebra counterpart exists at TauCeti/Algebra/Homology/AInfinity/Algebra/Hom/Iso.lean:154 `theorem linearPart_inverse_bijective`; grep finds no such lemma in Module/Right/Hom/Inverse.lean.
findings.fix: Add `theorem linearPart_inverse_bijective (f) (hf) : Function.Bijective (f.inverse hf).linearPart` (proof: rewrite with `linearPart_inverse`, then `.symm.bijective`).
findings.issue: No `linearPart_inverse_bijective`: `inverse_inverse` needs `h : Function.Bijective (f.inverse hf).linearPart`, and users have no lemma to build it, so they must unfold `linearPart_inverse` themselves to form `(f.inverse hf).inverse _`.

findings.evidence: TauCeti/Algebra/Homology/AInfinity/Algebra/Hom/Iso.lean:199-255 defines `IsIso` and these lemmas for `AInfinityHom`; grep for `IsIso` under Module/ finds only `IsQuasiIso`.
findings.fix: Add `AInfinityRightModuleHom.IsIso` with an unexposed body, plus `isIso_def`, `isIso_id` (simp), `IsIso.comp`, `isIso_of_linearPart_bijective`, `isIso_inverse`, `IsIso.linearPart_bijective`, `isIso_iff_linearPart_bijective` and `IsIso.isQuasiIso`, matching the algebra file. Then restate the two headline theorems as `isIso_iff_linearPart_bijective` and `isIso_iff_isQuasiIso_of_differential_eq_zero`.
findings.issue: No `IsIso` predicate for module morphisms. `exists_inverse_iff_linearPart_bijective` (line 151) and `exists_inverse_iff_isQuasiIso_of_differential_eq_zero` (line 186) both spell out `∃ g, g.comp f = id ∧ f.comp g = id` by hand, and there is no `isIso_id`, `IsIso.comp`, `isIso_inverse` or `IsIso.isQuasiIso`. The roadmap's 'uniqueness up to isomorphism' for modules needs this notion.

summary: The module inverse API is missing two parts of the algebra API it says it follows: the bijectivity lemma for the inverse's unary component, and an `IsIso` predicate with its basic lemmas, so consumers have to restate the two-sided-inverse existential by hand.
